name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.157.0 — The mocks seed derives its own records instead of asking for the client's. design/mocks/records/<entity>.json is a plain JSON array of at least three record objects, derived by the session from the seed's Product and Facts, the research brief and anything under design/mocks/references/; the {provenance: real|synthetic, records: [...]} wrapper and every check on where the data came from are gone, and an object wrapping the records is refused so there is one shape to derive and one refusal to read. Mock data is invented by definition, so no refusal sends the session to a human for it: the SEED step and every records remedy now say derive, never ask. The journey-drawn check that screens must carry the seed's values is unchanged. 7.156.0 — The design seed asks for three records with a declared origin, never three of the client's real records: each design/mocks/records/<entity>.json is now {"provenance": "real"|"synthetic", "records": [...]}, so a pre-launch product with no customers tags its invented records synthetic and passes SEED — where the real-only gate left it with no legitimate input at all. The three-record floor, the wireframe record-hit check, and the preference for the client's own records are unchanged; the accepted seed-done mark now discloses each entity's provenance. 7.155.0 — An exclusion answer stays the client's to change until the work is signed off, with a Change answer control on every answered row before then and a dated read-only record and 409 refusal after; a taken-back client request can be put back on the walk page, the client index, and the exclusion row it produced; and confirming a journey now shows an immediate receipt instead of looking like nothing happened.
